views.name: movies_base
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  id,
  title,
  year,
  date_published,
  duration,
  country,
  worlwide_gross_income,
  languages,
  production_company
FROM movies
views.description: Normalized projection of the movies table: preserves original movie identifiers and attributes, parses/standardizes some fields where safe (keeps worlwide_gross_income as original text because values are not reliably numeric). Use this as a clean movie dimension for joins and downstream aggregations. | Use for: Join movies to ratings, genres, directors, or cast; Filter movies by year/country/language/duration ranges; Compute aggregates per movie or per production_company

views.name: names_base
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  id,
  name,
  height,
  date_of_birth,
  known_for_movies
FROM names
views.description: Normalized projection of the names table: one row per person preserving original identifiers and attributes. Use as the people/person dimension for joins to role_mapping or director_mapping. | Use for: List people who worked on a movie or were directors; Compute average height/age distributions of cast/directors; Join person attributes to movie-level aggregates

views.name: movie_ratings
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  movie_id,
  avg_rating,
  total_votes,
  median_rating
FROM ratings
views.description: Per-movie rating facts: one row per movie_id with rating measures. Use for joins to movies to filter/sort by avg_rating, total_votes, or median_rating. | Use for: Top-rated movies by avg_rating or total_votes; Filter movies with minimum number of votes; Join ratings to movies for enrichment

views.name: movie_genres
views.description: One row per (movie_id, genre) as recorded in the genre table. Use this for counting genres per movie, filtering movies by genre, or joining to movies while being aware of row multiplication. | Use for: List movies in a given genre; Count number of genres per movie; Aggregate movies by genre

views.name: movie_directors
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  dm.movie_id,
  dm.name_id,
  n.name
FROM director_mapping dm
LEFT JOIN names n ON dm.name_id = n.id
views.description: Denormalized mapping of movies to director people: one row per (movie_id, name_id) from director_mapping, joined to names to include the director's name. Use for queries that need director names with movie keys. | Use for: List directors for a movie or list movies by director; Aggregate movies per director; Join director names into movie-centric reports

views.name: movie_cast
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  rm.movie_id,
  rm.name_id,
  rm.category,
  n.name
FROM role_mapping rm
LEFT JOIN names n ON rm.name_id = n.id
views.description: Denormalized cast mapping: one row per (movie_id, name_id, category) from role_mapping, joined to names to include person name. Preserves cast category (e.g., actor/actress) for filtering. | Use for: List cast members for a movie; Count cast size per movie; Filter cast by category and join person attributes

views.name: movies_with_ratings
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  m.id,
  m.title,
  m.year,
  m.date_published,
  m.duration,
  m.country,
  m.worlwide_gross_income,
  m.languages,
  m.production_company,
  r.avg_rating,
  r.total_votes,
  r.median_rating
FROM movies m
LEFT JOIN ratings r ON m.id = r.movie_id
views.description: Left-joined movie dimension enriched with ratings measures. One row per movie.id with rating fields added when available. Use this as the primary wide movie relation for ranking or filtering by ratings. | Use for: Rank movies by rating or votes; Filter movies by rating thresholds; Compute correlation between duration and rating

views.name: movie_top_rank_by_rating
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  m.id,
  m.title,
  r.avg_rating,
  r.total_votes,
  RANK() OVER (ORDER BY r.avg_rating DESC, r.total_votes DESC) AS rating_rank
FROM movies m
LEFT JOIN ratings r ON m.id = r.movie_id
views.description: Per-movie rank by avg_rating then total_votes (descending): one row per movie.id with a rank value. Do not hardcode a top-K; downstream queries should filter on rank <= K. Use for top-N movie queries compatible with ties. | Use for: Select top-K movies by rating or votes; Examine ties in rating-based rankings; Create paginated leaderboards of movies

views.name: movie_genre_counts
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  movie_id,
  COUNT(DISTINCT genre) AS genre_count
FROM genre
GROUP BY movie_id
views.description: Counts of genres per movie: one row per movie_id with the number of distinct genres. Useful for filtering movies by genre multiplicity or analyzing multi-genre distribution. | Use for: Find movies with many genres; Filter to single-genre movies; Join genre counts to movie attributes
